note: Districts filled by a best guess (decision 56): places the written record describes as built up, where no atlas plate could be placed and the borough as a whole shows no deficit against the census. 'shares' is the lead's best guess of the share of the district's street-front lots that carried a building in each year; it is NOT a measured figure. Outlines are drawn from today's street positions (Overture), generous at the water (the generator keeps lots off water, beach and parks).

properties.name: Coney Island (West Brighton and the West End)
properties.basis: best guess: the railroads reached West Brighton in 1875-79; hotels, pavilions and bathhouses lined Surf Avenue and the Bowery in the 1880s; Steeplechase Park 1897, Luna Park 1903, Dreamland 1904; the subway reached Stillwell Avenue in 1920; the West End was cleared for housing in the 1950s-70s. The plates of the 1907 atlas for this part could not be placed.

properties.name: Rockaway Beach (Seaside, Hammels, Holland)
properties.basis: best guess: the railroad across Jamaica Bay opened in 1880; Seaside and Hammels were resorts of hotels, bathhouses and pavilions in the 1880s (Seaside burned in 1892 and was rebuilt); bungalows and boarding houses filled the streets 1900-1920; much was cleared for Shore Front Parkway (1939) and for housing in the 1950s-70s.

properties.name: Arverne and Edgemere
properties.basis: best guess: Arverne-by-the-Sea was laid out by Remington Vernam in 1888, Edgemere in 1892; hotels, then streets of frame cottages and bungalows by 1910-1920; fire of 1922; the district was cleared for an urban renewal area in the late 1960s and stood empty for decades.

properties.name: Inwood (Tubby Hook and the Kingsbridge Road)
properties.basis: best guess: Tubby Hook, a village at the Hudson River Railroad's station (1847) at the foot of Dyckman Street, a few dozen frame houses by the 1860s; farmhouses, estates and institutions along the Kingsbridge Road (Broadway); the district was built up only after the subway of 1906, when the apartment houses replaced them. The plate of the 1897 atlas could not be registered.
